notes:
Acyclic map reached (iter-3 had 2 direct + 4 indirect U/D cycles: Billing<->Complaints, Billing<->Scheduling, Complaints->T&S->Scheduling->Complaints, Pricing->Scheduling->Reviews->Pricing; iter-4 has none, 0 rule warnings). How the cycles were broken:
(a) Billing<->Complaints: Complaints becomes a client of Billing's refund/charge API (Billing upstream). Sound: matches the stated fact 'Billing knows how to reverse a charge, Complaints just says refund lesson L, amount A'.
(b) Billing<->Scheduling (failed hold): Billing calls Scheduling's cancel, so Scheduling stays upstream. Sound API-client move, but the whole failed-hold flow is improvised (R3 Q5, R5 Q1); the facts only say the pre-auth is 'just Stripe holding money'.
(c) Pricing->Scheduling->Reviews->Pricing: Scheduling carries the completed-lesson count in the quote request (sound carry-data move; the facts mention '>=100 lessons' but not the source, so the 'completed lessons' answer is improvised). Then Reviews<->Scheduling (search needs rating, Reviews needs lesson outcomes) was resolved by making Scheduling an API client pushing outcomes into Reviews' OHS, justified by the improvised R6 answer 'Community decides that only held lessons get a review request'. Defensible, but weaker: a context that consumes outcome facts is usually downstream; the 'who decides eligibility' question was asked specifically to justify the flip.
(d) Complaints->T&S->Scheduling->Complaints: flipped to T&S upstream of Complaints. The R5 question was a leading either/or ('Does Trust & Safety set what that report must contain ... or does it take whatever Complaints sends?'); the critic caught it and the facilitator re-asked, but the 'neutral' re-ask asked 'Who came up with the categories and severity levels?', presupposing the categories the expert had just improvised. The facts only say Complaints says 'complaint upheld against tutor X'; the category/severity contract is entirely improvised, so this flip is contaminated by the earlier leading question even though it does not contradict any stated fact.
No direction contradicts a stated fact. Heavy reliance on improvisation (~15 [improvised] answers), but all are listed as 'to re-confirm', which is honest. The expert was never shown candidate flips and asked to choose; the facilitator decided and reported afterwards (assertion 8 passes only because nothing is kept).
Regressions vs iter-3 / trainer rules: (1) Stripe is now [OHS,PL]->[ACL] although the expert facts say 'Stripe's API is an industry standard; we're happy to follow it' -> CF was the right call (iter-3 had CF). (2) No Customer/Supplier relationship anywhere although the trainer rule is 'C/S between internal teams' and all teams are internal; every internal link is OHS/PL->ACL (iter-3 used C/S, which caused validator ACL-in-C/S warnings, possibly why they were dropped). Missing Pricing->Billing link: the facts say 'Billing needs the price/fee calculation', handled only via the improvised locked-quote snapshot.
Eval critique: assertion 8 is weak (an acyclic map passes even if the facilitator, not the expert, picked every flip); add assertions for CF towards Stripe and C/S between internal teams, and one penalising cycle resolutions grounded only in [improvised] answers. Timing: 960.7s, 228,366 tokens (vs 223.4s/75,140 for baseline).
